newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil high court suspends cell phone vote.
newsitem.headline: Brazil high court suspends cell phone vote.

text.p: Brazil's highest Court voted unanimously on Wednesday that the Ministry of Communications could act as the industry's regulator, thus rejecting an opposition claim that it was unconstitutional, an official said.
Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) president Sepulveda Pertence then suspended further voting on a case brought against the country's telecommunications law until a later date.

The opposition challenge to Article 13 of the Minimum Telecommunications Law, which gives the Communications Ministry regulatory power over the industry until an independent regulatory agency is created, is considered the most important in the case brought against the law.
The tribunal must still rule on a series of other articles, but analysts say decisions on those are unlikely to interrupt Brazil's telecommunications privatization process.
At least 12 multinational consortia are due to bid on April 7 for concessions to run 10 Band B cellular service areas across the country.
The government expects to raise between $5.0 billion to $6.0 billion from the Band B tenders.
The tribunal set no new date to resume voting on the application for an injunction.
